findings.title: Do not accept view scope for group management
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view permission on all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing groups to the top level. A read-only administrator can therefore mutate the group hierarchy. Require MANAGE here and add a test that an all-groups VIEW grant cannot POST groups.

findings.title: Resolve actual group IDs when constructing the user-search filter
findings.body: This enumeration treats authorization resource IDs as GroupModel IDs, but AdminPermissionsSchema creates resources with generated IDs and stores the group ID in the resource name. hasPermission() then looks up that generated ID by name, and the returned set also contains generated IDs rather than group IDs. In particular, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant matches the synthetic Groups resource and returns its authorization ID; UsersResource installs that nonempty set as UserModel.GROUPS, filtering out every actual member. Individual resources created by getOrCreateResource() also have no Groups type set, so this type query does not enumerate them. Resolve real groups (including the all-groups case), evaluate using their IDs, and return actual group IDs; cover both user search and count with group-member grants.
